# Shared STE-inspired writing profile

## Purpose and selected principles

Curators and explainer authors use this single profile for invariant statements, family guarantees,
history reasons and walkthrough prose. It selects clarity principles from
[ASD-STE100](https://asd-ste100.org/about_STE.html); it does not claim full ASD-STE100 compliance,
an "80 percent" measurement or a new controlled-language standard.

Name the actor and use concrete verbs: say who must do what, not merely that something is handled.
Write one independently testable promise per invariant. A paragraph develops one idea. Sentences
normally target about 20–25 words; precision takes priority over sentence length. Keep an exact
technical identifier or essential qualification even when the sentence is longer. Never split an
invariant automatically to meet a word target: a split is an explicit authored semantic change.

State conditions and exceptions explicitly. Keep quantifiers and negation: "every", "only", "no"
and "must not" are part of the obligation, not words to trim. Repeat the same term for the same
concept. Prefer a short explanation to an invented synonym.

## Use the project's vocabulary

Read applicable existing term records and use the product's vocabulary; do not create a second
terminology registry. These explanations orient the author without replacing those records:

| Term | Use |
| --- | --- |
| invariant | One independently testable obligation, with its applicability, conditions and exclusions. |
| family | An authored record whose members support its own joint guarantee; not a directory grouping. |
| joint guarantee | What the members together promise that none promises alone. Do not concatenate their statements. |
| realization | An attributed code place that carries an obligation, with its own rationale and role. |
| proof | Recorded evidence of a particular tested facet; not a claim that every case is established. |
| history row | The existing writer's content-bound judgment about a subject and its change. |
| revision | The exact record version the judgment or comparison addresses; never a prose edit counter supplied by the author. |
| candidate | The exact proposed code and memory state under examination, not an assumed installed or landed state. |

Keep identifiers, quoted source text and admitted effect labels exact. Distinguish
missing, unexamined, unavailable and measured absence: respectively not supplied, not checked,
not readable/obtainable, and checked with no instance found in a stated scope. None establishes
another, and none proves equivalence.

## Separate the promise from its support

State the promise in `statement`. Keep applicability, essential conditions and exclusions in their
existing semantic fields. When the statement relies on those fields, make that connection clear;
read the statement and scope together. Do not remove a condition just because another display shows it.

Keep realizations, proofs, identities and authoring provenance in their existing structural owners.
A history reason explains the concrete change and its consequence; a task ID or "wording improved"
alone explains neither. Use the existing [handoff contract](../templates/curator-handoff-list.md):
producer-owned fields remain verbatim, including the original statement and evidence. Author a
proposed record rewrite separately; do not silently replace the statement the producer handed over.
The writer continues to own IDs, anchors, revisions and row mechanics.

## Independent meaning review before publication

Use the existing [independent fact-check](../criteria/onboarding-memory.md#om-2--independent-fact-check-of-curated-knowledge-second-reader-requirement-bound-mik-r53-rule-5),
not a style-specific gate. A clearer rewrite is never proof of preserved meaning.

1. Preserve the exact old revision, before text, semantic scope, source anchors and evidence identities.
   Bind the proposed text to that baseline and the exact candidate being examined.
2. Compare old and new actor, trigger, required behavior, forbidden behavior, quantifiers, conditions and exclusions.
   Name each facet explicitly, including an unchanged field that the new statement depends on.
3. A reader who wrote none of the drafts explains each promise without oral repair and checks
   concrete conforming, violating and boundary cases against both versions. The reader records
   each ambiguity, changed obligation, missing evidence and unresolved case, not just a verdict.
4. Propose `clarify` only after independent review establishes that the obligation stays the same.
   A real change uses the existing appropriate effect and writer/history/revision route. Do not
   classify an edit from its apparent size or its word count. A family change retains its own
   authored effect, guarantee, examined members and writer-owned revision.
5. Correct or explicitly classify every disputed case before the normal writer publishes.
   An ambiguous draft stays unaccepted and names the actor, quantifier, condition or case in dispute.
   An unreadable revision or missing evidence is a reported gap, never an equivalence judgment.

### Worked comparison and deliberate failures (illustrations, not pilot evidence)

Before: "For every landing, the landing owner must publish only the accepted code and memory trees;
if either tree differs from the accepted candidate, publication must be refused."

Proposed: "For every landing, the landing owner must publish only the accepted code and memory trees.
The owner must refuse publication if either tree differs from the accepted candidate."

The proposed draft names the same actor, every landing, the same allowed trees and the same refusal
trigger. Its author has not accepted equivalence. The independent reader must test at least these cases:

| Case | Required reading of both versions |
| --- | --- |
| Conforming | Both trees equal the accepted candidate: the owner may publish under the existing admission rules. This promise alone does not grant admission. |
| Violating | The owner publishes a different memory tree even though the code tree matches: the owner violates the refusal. |
| Boundary | Only one tree differs: "either" still requires refusal. No exception for a code-only match exists. |

| Draft fault | What the independent comparison must catch |
| --- | --- |
| Removed negation | Changing "must not publish a different tree" to "must publish a different tree" reverses forbidden behavior. |
| Changed quantifier | Replacing "every landing" with "normally at landing" permits previously forbidden exceptions. It is not a clarification. |
| Lost condition | Dropping "if either tree differs" changes the refusal trigger; removing it from scope or omitting its connection in the prose does not preserve it. |
| Unrecorded effect | Calling a changed obligation cosmetic, or publishing it without the appropriate authored effect and history route, leaves the change unaccepted. |
| Altered frozen row | Editing an old closed row to make the draft appear historical changes evidence, not meaning preservation. Retain the original bytes and use the normal new revision route. |

## Three-real-invariant pilot and adoption

Select three existing invariant revisions: a direct promise, a conditional or exception-bearing
promise, and an obligation used in an authored family guarantee. Preserve the exact before text,
revision, scope, source/evidence identities and family membership where relevant. Produce proposed
rewrites and the facet/case comparison above. Record source availability separately from semantic
review: a stored evidence pointer is not evidence that the pointed-to report was read or rerun.

Prototype on real records in shared scratch clones, never the official checkout. Keep a frozen
baseline and separate drafts. An independent reader must judge all three; the author's own table
is a proposal, not acceptance. Correct or classify every ambiguity before the normal admitted
writer publishes. Do not run the writer merely to demonstrate style, rewrite frozen history,
backfill closed rows, or bulk-rewrite existing records. Scratch-clone preparation and later writer
execution require their normal authorization and isolation; this guide grants neither.

After adoption, new or revised invariant statements, family guarantees, history reasons and
walkthrough prose use this profile. Migration authors link it from their procedure before waves
start; preserve every other leaf's required guidance rather than adding a second writing guide.
Existing frozen records and closed history remain inspectable at their original identities.
Guide edits follow normal source/copy checks and curation. The normal skill-copy generator carries
this reference; its composition entry is reference metadata, not another meaning authority.

There is no automatic semantic validator here. Word-count and vocabulary heuristics cannot approve,
reject or classify meaning. Schema, identity, admission, invariant gates and normal writer refusal
and retry behavior remain unchanged. This profile provides author/reviewer guidance and examples,
not a language gate or a closeout bypass.

# Curator — writer and authoring step detail

Read the serving-build command section before a CLI deciding run or write. Read the remaining
authoring detail when you reach **Curation workflow 2: Before ingest**, not before.
Its family/external-reference formats and read-back call are used at **Curation workflow 3: Group only justified obligations**.
The operation owns serving-build authority; this file supplies the command and its report semantics.

## Step 2 — serving-build command and options

Prefer the mounted `knowledge_write`. For a CLI deciding run or write, bind the command to the
starting server's `server_info.servingBuild` as `operations/curation.md` requires. Obtain the
original interpreter from the role launch receipt's `toolServer.command[0]`, or the selected
server's startup definition's `command`. Preserve that spelling: `servingBuild.pythonExecutable`
is resolved and may point through a virtual-environment symlink to an interpreter without its
dependencies. If the admitted launch command is unavailable, report the CLI binding unavailable;
do not infer it from the resolved path or install another build.

Fill these values from that launch and the starting `server_info`, then print the CLI's identity:

```sh
AR_SERVING_PYTHON='<original admitted launch interpreter>'
AR_SERVING_PACKAGE='<server_info.servingBuild.packageRoot>'
AR_SERVING_PARENT="$(dirname -- "$AR_SERVING_PACKAGE")"
PYTHONPATH="$AR_SERVING_PARENT" "$AR_SERVING_PYTHON" -P -c \
  'import json; from agents_remember.serving.build_info import process_serving_build; print(json.dumps(process_serving_build().payload().model_dump(mode="json", exclude_none=True)))'
```

Compare its `version`, `sourceDigest`, `packageRoot`, `pythonExecutable` and `commit` with the
starting stamp before using this CLI to decide or write. A missing identity or a mismatch does
not establish the serving build. Report it; use the mounted tool when it admits the operation.
Keep an unreported commit unknown, never call it a verified clean checkout.

Use the same interpreter and explicit package path for the public CLI commands:

```sh
PYTHONPATH="$AR_SERVING_PARENT" "$AR_SERVING_PYTHON" -P -m agents_remember.cli \
  knowledge-worklist --contract '<this leaf enclosure contract>'
PYTHONPATH="$AR_SERVING_PARENT" "$AR_SERVING_PYTHON" -P -m agents_remember.cli \
  knowledge-ingest --contract '<this leaf enclosure contract>' \
  --list '<the hand-off list>' --authorization-ref '<the admitted authorization>' --commit --json
```

The worklist command computes and persists the leaf's worklist beside its contract. The writer
reads that worklist and the contract's code and memory roots. Without `--commit`, ingest plans,
validates and writes no files; `--commit` authorizes file writes, never a Git commit or acceptance.
The parser has no `--baseline`, `--publish` or `--publish-to` options. Read the actual report state,
written paths, record/entry IDs and refusals: exit zero covers both a plan and a write, and even a
`written` report with no written paths establishes no publication. A correct-input write refusal
uses the procedure linked from the operation's **Failure handling** section.

## Step 2 — check messages

(`realization_rationale_absent`).

The command
   needs converted memory: on the legacy format it refuses with `legacy-format` and names the conversion command.

## Step 2 — weakness and dependent records

**A weakness and a dependent are recorded through the writer, as every record.** An entry of kind `weakness` in a producer's hand-off list becomes a `WKN-` record through the writer, or the report says why not: the writer refuses one without a file, with an unknown kind, or with a statement beyond its one-sentence bound, and the refusal names the field. An entry of kind `dependent` becomes a `DPD-` record: the document, and for each place it stands on the recorded value the writer reads at the task's tip -- a code anchor, a whole file's blob, or an invariant's or a family's revision -- with the confirmation's task, role and commit. Every write of a dependent is a confirmation; no value is typed in. A Curator answers the worklist's row for a weakness (it stands, and the anchor moves with the code; or it is closed) and for a changed document (only the confirmed record answers it). Neither record ever refuses a task.

## Step 3 — family and external-reference format

When you restate a family's
guarantee, name the family in `history` as a `changed` row with your `effect`; the writer fills the
family's own revision.

An external document a card rests on is cited as an
   `external` reference target in the card's sidecar, never as a repository path with a Git blob. Name that
   document in the handoff evidence for the record's `origin`, so the evidence shows which external document
   each backed record rests on.

## Step 3 — read-back call fragment

the records `knowledge_read` with `view="family"` names over this leaf's memory worktree, opened with your own tools

# Curator — authoring (D301)

Read the relevant section before the named step. Existing detail-source names below mean the separately delivered workspace paths linked in the capsule, not literal filesystem paths.

## Before routing cards, writing trace rows and lifting decisions

Read the card detail file (`reference/curator-card-details.md`, at its capsule-linked workspace path) when you reach **Curation workflow 4: L3 is last resort**, not before.
Use the writer for sidecar JSON, with only its scoped correct-write recovery; read the card detail file (`reference/curator-card-details.md`, at its capsule-linked workspace path) when you reach **Curation workflow 4: L3 is last resort**, not before.
   - a changed file whose card was brought up to date is answered by an `onboarding_trace` row
     (row format (`reference/curator-card-details.md`, at its capsule-linked workspace path), read when you reach **Curation workflow 4: L3 is last resort**, not before) written through `knowledge-ingest`; the hand-off names the
     subject, the disposition and the reason, and the writer binds the row to the source files'
     content.
Read the card detail file (`reference/curator-card-details.md`, at its capsule-linked workspace path) when you reach **Curation workflow 4: L3 is last resort**, not before.
   **Lift the decisions that keep governing code.** On converted memory, turn each developer ruling
   and requirement-packet choice that still constrains code into a decision record with the
   alternatives it weighed; decisions that matter only within the task stay in the task. The hand-off
   template's "Decision records (MIK-R13)" section gives the fields and the rules.

## Before curation step 1

1. **Reconcile three ways.** The pass succeeds only when these three bodies agree, or every material
   divergence is surfaced directly to its answering seat under the Curation capsule's §Failure handling and §Handoff / exit rules:
   - the existing system's **current intent** — source, tests, onboarding contracts, entity
     boundaries, durable incident lessons;
   - the **ruled change intent** — the task, developer decisions, approved design notes, builder
     report, reviewer verdict;
   - the **implemented reality** — the complete fed change set and its verification evidence.

   **Cards say what is true now.** Decide each sentence of every card and its paired notes
   one by one, whatever its tense or location, dated sections included. Edit individual
   sentences; never replace a section or regenerate a card wholesale. When a sentence is
   true now, keep its wording, including true statements about retired things. Before
   narrowing or dropping a sentence, search the supplied source and memory for what
   supports it. Repair or withdraw every false claim in every current carrier found by a
   bounded search: the card body, paired notes and sibling cards. Repair the class, not just
   one example. Remove past accounts, including dated change notes, “former … was removed”
   and “The fix: …”, from the card and name them in that card's history row, written after
   the card's last edit.

## Before curation step 2

2. **Route the durable knowledge through the real writer.** The reconciliation's requirement-shaped items
   are authored knowledge, not onboarding prose. Every target in it carries its own authored `rationale` (why
   that place carries the obligation) and optionally a `role`, as `../templates/curator-handoff-list.md` states;
   the writer never generates a rationale and refuses a list with an unexplained target;
   read the writer detail file (`reference/curator-writer-details.md`, at its capsule-linked workspace path) when you reach **Curation workflow 2: Before ingest**, not before. The writer writes files in
   this leaf's memory worktree: records under `knowledge/`, `realizes` and `proves` entries in the file sidecars,
   and the leaf's history file. **Consume the report, not the exit status:** its state
   is `written`, `planned` or `refused`; a refused run wrote nothing and names every problem with its own reason.
   A partial hand-off therefore stays visible; it is never rounded up to "the batch went through".

## Before curation step 3

3. **Examine family coverage and author it as part of the same list.** For every scoped obligation, decide whether
   the evidence and the project's intent justify a joint obligation with others. Where they do, author a `family`
   record in the list's `records` section, as `../templates/curator-handoff-list.md` states: the family's **own**
   guarantee text, its members, its routes and its admission — one obligation may belong to several families.
   Nothing is grouped by directory, route, label or shared anchor. A member or membership change **prompts a fresh
   look at the affected recorded guarantee**: update the stored family record only where that is justified, answer
   the family's worklist item with a history row that says what was examined. Read
   the writer detail file (`reference/curator-writer-details.md`, at its capsule-linked workspace path) when you reach **Curation workflow 2: Before ingest**, not before.
   Never let an implementation
   change rewrite member intent or family meaning by itself. Read the result
   back — the writer's report, and the records named by the read-back call (file `reference/curator-writer-details.md`, at its capsule-linked workspace path; read that file when you reach **Curation workflow 2: Before ingest**, not before) — and
   carry the coverage into the handoff: the families authored or updated, and those examined and left unchanged.

## Before curation step 4

4. **Route every change-set item and every notes item to the right home** through the
   `c-05-create-or-update-onboarding-files` skill workflow:
   - changed source files → their file-level cards and sidecars with compact current contracts;
     on converted memory, record the judgment in the history row. A mechanical consumer change
     with no contract impact gets a precise reviewed no-impact row, not invented architecture prose;
   - route overviews → body updates when route meaning changed, otherwise an explicit reviewed
     no-impact history entry only when that overview was reviewed;
   - entity catalog → only for real load-bearing entity changes;
   - a notes item with no file, route, or entity home → the L3 Operational-Notes target, **last
     resort only**, never the default drop point for an inconvenient finding;
   - generated route indexes → regenerate with `route_index_refresh` on `agents-remember-task` scoped to this leaf.

## Before curation step 5

5. **Reject overview-dumping and task-log-dumping.** Never add an overview heading named for a leaf or date;
   update the overview body that owns the meaning. Preserve a truth when it is important to future
   correctness, non-obvious, and expensive to rediscover. Omit code narration, temporary branch
   facts, raw test totals, generic implementation-round chronology, and facts obvious from code and
   tests.

# Correct-input write refusal — the same-tool ladder

Read this procedure when a writer or record tool refuses a correct write. Use the primary tool
first. If the refusal names a fault in your input, correct that input through the same tool.
A missing tool or unadmitted capability is not a refused correct write; report that missing
capability and what remains unwritten.

For a correct-input write refusal (D627; D631 Q25–Q26):

1. **Check the build and route.** Compare the serving build, the invoked build and the admitted
   target and input shape. Retain the tool's actual refusal. For the Curator's CLI binding, use
   the command procedure in `curator-writer-details.md`.
2. **Take an honest route the tool admits.** Keep the claim true, the serving build and the
   target authority. Record each input and refusal; a route that requires hidden edits, an older
   build lacking a check, false tool authorship or a weakened false claim is no route.
3. **Otherwise make that write openly by hand.** Tell the record's or machine state's owner
   before writing. This exception covers only the same tool and input class that refused;
   every other write still uses its tool. Record the manual write and its provenance, run every
   check that still works, and record the defect in an issue row. Put the tool, every input tried,
   every refusal, the actual write, all check results and that issue row in the full report. Claim no
   tool receipt for the manual work. The tool repair is a separate task when the developer slots it; the next Curator
   re-records the affected knowledge.

When admitted to your role, the covered record writes are `knowledge_write` or admitted
`knowledge-ingest`, `citation_fix`,
`citation_note_revision`, `curator_coherence` publish and `task_doc` edits, including
`append_decision`, `begin_review`, `record_review` and `record_route_review`.

For a refused correct `task_doc` edit, record the attempted inputs and refusal, notify the owner,
and amend the canonical document openly. The owner's next `task_doc` publication refreshes
renders and projections; rendered copies are never parsed back. The decided task-folder exception
similarly covers only the refused retirement or movement step, never a Git commit or another
transaction step. This procedure gives Bootstrap no new writer, task-document or migration duty.

**The stops remain.** Read, check, validation and sync refusals, starts, product guards and commit
gates retain their boundaries. Repair validator and gate findings under D229; this write ladder
does not waive them. A denied or unanswered permission request is not worked around through
another tool, command, helper or later turn (D632). Other tools and input classes retain their
normal routes.
